content: Lipgloss/viewport ANSI pitfalls: (1) Ghost lines (issue #1477) — stale ANSI content in viewport causes uncleared cells when content changes; wide runes and ANSI sequences mess with cell counts. (2) Never use len() or len([]rune()) for string width — use ansi.StringWidth or lipgloss.Width() which are ANSI-aware. (3) Forcing color profile with lipgloss.SetColorProfile(termenv.TrueColor) outputs ANSI in non-TTY environments. (4) ANSI-aware truncation: use reflow's truncate.String not naive string slicing. (5) On Windows, only initial terminal width is known — after resize the renderer can't compensate since SIGWINCH is not supported. (6) HighPerformanceRendering option improves rendering in terminals with heavy ANSI usage. (7) Overlay composition requires tracking escape sequences across boundary — preserve sequences that 'cross under' overlay.
